id_and_class.summary: Marilyn Schlitz treats consciousness as an interface that entangles inner subjective experience with outer, observable behavior and events. When the boundary between inner and outer becomes more fluid, she suggests, minds may tap shared and possibly non-local fields of information, which would account for psi, mystical experience, and reported contact with the dead.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as an Interface Between Inner and Outer

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is an entanglement of inner and outer existence, the interface linking what it feels like to be someone with how that person behaves and reacts.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Inner experience and outer phenomena are interwoven through the interface Schlitz calls the Theory of Mind (ToM). Drawing on quantum holography and some forms of panpsychism, she suggests consciousness is not wholly confined to the brain.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: ToM includes the ordinary capacity to attribute beliefs, intentions, emotions, and knowledge to oneself and others, which grounds empathy and social foresight.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: An inner subjective domain; an outer objective domain; an interface between them; shared, possibly non-local informational fields.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Laboratory, clinical, and field research on psi and healing, along with first-person reports from altered states and psychomantium sessions.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Subjective experience, Social cognition, Psi, Altered and mystical states, After-death communication
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Psi as extreme sensitivity of the ToM interface, possibly working through unconscious or non-local information processing when the boundary between subjective and objective loosens.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Partly non-local: Schlitz suggests consciousness may be entangled or shared across individuals.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: ToM lets people handle social life with empathy and foresight by linking inner states to observable behavior. In heightened form it may give access to information beyond the senses.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Minds may draw on shared informational fields when inner and outer boundaries become fluid.
core_claims_and_evidence: Consciousness links subjective experience with objective behavior and events.
Psi, altered states, and mystical experiences may arise when the boundary between subjective and objective domains becomes more fluid.

In Schlitz’s psychomantium and virtual-reality studies, people engaging imaginatively with departed loved ones report veridical experiences across sight, sound, smell, and bodily sensation, with therapeutic benefit.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Empirical (experimental and field research on psi and healing) and experiential reports

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Psychomantium sessions and virtual-reality studies of contact with deceased loved ones.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Some researchers dismiss psi as anomalous or pseudoscientific, which leaves the model’s main explanatory target in dispute.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The model is offered as a potential explanation; Schlitz does not specify how the interface accesses non-local fields or how quantum holography would apply.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Schlitz suggests the model could explain veridical after-death encounters and expanded consciousness beyond the physical world, without asserting survival outright.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Schlitz holds that the ToM opens a window onto the interconnectedness of all life.

related_theories.name: Near Death Experiences, Survival, Past Lives

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Schlitz’s Theory of Mind (Landscape of Consciousness), Marilyn Schlitz
